experiment_name: Max-N PUCT runtime at 4/16/32 simulations on an identical state

algorithm_config.component: MaxNPUCT via scripts/monopolyzero_sim_runtime.py (reuses monopoly_bench.cli.smoke()'s exact state-construction code)

result: All three simulation counts (4, 16, 32) returned a legal action from the identical starting state, with latency scaling roughly linearly (0.069s -> 0.111s -> 0.222s), consistent with per-simulation cost being dominated by env clone + forward pass. Same chosen action at every count on this particular state - not a general claim about action-choice sensitivity to simulation count.
notes: integrity.fallbacks is null (not applicable, same reasoning as 008 - masked search has no fallback path). peak_rss_gib is null (not separately measured for this run).
